column2: There are many ancestor gods you may choose to honour. Will it be Grungni, Ancestor God of mining and smithcraft? Or his beloved wife Valaya, Ancestor Goddess of healing and protection? Grimnir the Fearless, the mighty warrior god, and wise Thungni, patron of runesmithing, also wield great power.

The Ungol pantheon holds many gods you may follow. Will it be Great Ursun, Father of Bears? Or Dazh the sun of plenty, who holds the good of men at heart? Perhaps mighty Tor, god of thunder and war? Or the trickster Kalita, patron of merchants and liars?

The Nehekharan pantheon holds many gods you may follow. Golden Ptra, the Great Creator and god of the sun, or vengeful Asaph, the Beautiful Asp and goddess of magic? Perhaps righteous Phakth, the Hawk of Justice and god of the sky? Or faceless Usirian, Lord and Master of the Underworld...
I pledge my axe to Grungni. I would give my life for his honour!
May Grimnir the Fearless bring strength to my arm!
Hallowed be Mother Valaya!
Wise Thungni, share your secrets with me, and I shall keep them.
It shall be Ursun. May the Bear protect me.
Dazzling Dazh watches over me!
Kalita will bless me with riches beyond imagining.
I will do battle in mighty Tor's name!
Ptra rules over them all!
O beautiful Asaph. May the Asp protect me.
I will bring righteous justice in Phakth's name!
May Usirian bestow the secrets of the afterlife upon me.
Grimnir is the Ancestor God of warriors and patron of the Slayer cult, who bore the Axe of Grimnir. He marched north to close the great gate spewing Chaos into the world, and never returned.

Valaya is the Ancestor Goddess of healing and protector of the hearth, armed with the rune axe Peacegiver. Her priests and priestesses tend the sick and perform the rites of marriage and birth. Her name wards against sorcery, and her runes are worn as protective talismans.

Grungni is the Ancestor God of mining and smithcraft, and the most important god of the dawi. He was the first to delve into the rock, to mine the ores and smelt them into metal, and he taught the dawi to do the same. So he gave them the tools and the means to defend themselves against their foes.

Thungni is the god of runic magic and runesmithing. The dawi say he went deep into the earth during the Long Migration and spent long years in a place he named Ankor Bryn, the Glittering Realm. When he came back he brought the secret of runic magic to the dawi.

Ursun, the Father of Bears, is often shown as a cave bear with a crown and teeth and claws of glistening gold. He can take the form of a man too: burly and bearded, with a weathered face, thick hairy arms, a great mop of hair and nothing but a loincloth.

Dazh is the god of the sun and of plenty. He is shown as a handsome young man with golden hair and shining eyes, his body wreathed in fire. So dazzling is he that none can look upon him without being blinded.
Kalita is the god of merchants, money and liars, and of all goods traded and bartered. He is said to steal the warmth of Dazh to shelter the trading ventures of those he favours.
Tor is the god of thunder and lightning and a god of warriors. He is shown as a muscled, square-jawed warrior with a great axe hafted in oak, with which he cleaves the sky to loose the thunderbolts.

Ptra is the Nehekharan god of the sun, the first to set foot upon the world. He is the great creator and stands for immortality and eternity. Alone among the gods he has no animal form and always appears as a man, but his eyes hold all the stars of the sky, and his gaze is enough to drive a man mad.

Asaph, the vengeful Nehekharan goddess of magic and beauty, is a powerful mistress. She hears the call of those who seek vengeance for a grievous wrong. Asaph sometimes takes the form of an asp, and even then she is lovely.
Phakth is the Nehekharan god of the sky and of justice. He is a muscular man with the head of a hawk, and may also appear as a great blue-banded hawk with golden eyes.

Those who worship faceless Usirian have chosen an enigmatic master. The Lord of the Underworld is a harsh judge, but he shares the secrets of the afterlife with those who honour the dead. He is never pictured, for that is sacrilege, but his name is called again and again in the Nehekharan rites of burial.
I hope to prove myself worthy.
You have worked devoutly to walk the path of Valaya. In her name you have promoted peace and understanding among your subjects. Your diplomatic skill has grown for it.
You have worked devoutly to walk the path of Ursun. In his name you have inspired respect and awe in your subjects. Your diplomatic skill has grown for it.
You have worked devoutly to walk the path of Grimnir. In his name you have practised your axework and spent many hours over the war table with your captains. Your martial skill has grown for it.
You have worked devoutly to walk the path of Tor. In his name you have practised your axework and spent many hours over the war table with your captains. Your martial skill has grown for it.
You have worked devoutly to walk the path of Phakth. In his name you have practised your swordwork and spent many hours over the war table with your captains. Your martial skill has grown for it.

You have worked devoutly to walk the path of Grungni. In his name you have sent out many good mining expeditions and spent long hours in the mines of [Root.Capital.GetName]. Your stewardship has grown for it.

You have worked devoutly to walk the path of Dazh. In his name you have held harvest festivals and fertility rites and spent long hours in the fields of [Root.Capital.GetName]. Your stewardship has grown for it.

You have worked devoutly to walk the path of Ptra. In his name you have travelled the realm to inspect the great necropolises and temples of old and paid for several expeditions. Your stewardship has grown for it.
You have worked devoutly to walk the path of Kalita. In his name you have plotted against your trade rivals, spread accusations and pulled strings. Your skill at intrigue has grown for it.
You have worked devoutly to walk the path of Usirian. In his name you have learned the secrets of the afterlife and outwitted tomb robbers with cunning alone. Your skill at intrigue has grown for it.
You have worked devoutly to walk the path of Thungni. In his name you have sought out knowledge and studied the history of the runes. Your learning has grown for it.

You have worked devoutly to walk the path of Asaph. In her name you have sought out knowledge and secrets, both in the mortal world and in her own domain, the Realm of Magic. Your learning has grown for it.
I hope to be worthy of this blessing.

Many find it odd that a [Root.GetTitle] works in the mines, but striking the rock makes you feel closer to Grungni than any prayer. As you rest you see [From.GetTitledFirstName] coming, and you talk a while about the new seams. It turns out [From.GetSheHe] is a follower of Grungni too!

It is a fine day and you are training with the axe. Over your midday ale you fall into a talk about axes with [From.GetTitledFirstName], and it turns out [From.GetSheHe] is a devout follower of Grimnir too. The longer you talk, the more you seem to have in common!

It is early morning and you are at the shrine of Valaya, deep in prayer. You hear soft footsteps behind you. Who could it be at this hour? [From.GetTitledFirstName], as it turns out. You exchange some pleasantries and soon you are deep in talk. You have so much in common!

It is early morning and you are studying a statue of Thungni, deep in thought. You hear soft footsteps behind you. Who could it be at this hour? [From.GetTitledFirstName], as it turns out. You exchange some pleasantries and soon you are deep in talk. You have so much in common!

It is early morning and you are at the shrine of Ursun, deep in prayer. You hear heavy footsteps behind you. Who could it be at this hour? [From.GetTitledFirstName], as it turns out. You exchange some pleasantries and soon you are deep in talk. You have so much in common!

Many find it odd that a [Root.GetTitle] works in the fields, but tending the land makes you feel closer to Dazh than any prayer. As you rest you see [From.GetTitledFirstName] coming, and you talk a while about the harvest. It turns out [From.GetSheHe] is a follower of Dazh too!

When you needed an accomplice in a small scheme, [From.GetTitledFirstName] proved an unexpected ally. Think what shared profit can do to unite two souls! It was pure business at first, but you have much in common, not least your reverence for Kalita. Now you spend more time talking than plotting...

It is a fine day and you are out hunting with a small party. Over your midday meal you fall into a talk about bows with [From.GetTitledFirstName], and it turns out [From.GetSheHe] is a devout follower of Tor too. The longer you talk, the more you seem to have in common!

Many find it odd that a [Root.GetTitle] walks the streets of the city alone, but watching over your realm makes you feel closer to Ptra than any prayer. As you rest you see [From.GetTitledFirstName] coming, and you talk a while about the flood and the harvest. It turns out [From.GetSheHe] is a follower of Ptra too!

It is early morning and you are at the temple of Asaph, deep in prayer. You hear soft footsteps behind you. Who could it be at this hour? [From.GetTitledFirstName], as it turns out. You exchange some pleasantries and soon you are deep in talk. You have so much in common!

You are out hunting a band of petty tomb robbers. While you rest to study the ground, you fall into a talk about the foundations of justice with [From.GetTitledFirstName]. It turns out [From.GetSheHe] is a follower of Phakth too. The longer you talk, the more you seem to have in common!

When you needed an accomplice in a small scheme, [From.GetTitledFirstName] proved an unexpected ally. It was pure business at first, but you have much in common, not least your reverence for Usirian and the secrets of the dead. Now you spend more time talking than plotting...
[From.GetFirstName], we should talk some more!
Keep talking with §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§!.\n
Enough talk. Back to prayer.

You sit huddled together by the fire, the air thick with tension. The sky outside is black with clouds and Tor's presence is as real as the rain drumming on the roof. Suddenly the room is lit by a blinding flash and a deafening crack splits the silence. Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] bursts into tears.
Fear not, for the god of thunder is our protector!
Run out into the storm to show §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! that thunder is nothing to fear.\n
Let me tell you a story...
You tell §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! a story about mighty Tor.\n
Your cowardice shames you, [From.GetFirstName]!
Scold §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! for [From.GetHerHis] cowardice.\n

As you gaze at a beautiful statue of Asaph, passion stirs in you, and your eyes find [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s across the room. For a moment the whole world falls silent. The fire burns to your very core...
Tonight I shall bed [From.GetFirstName] in the name of Asaph.
This is... something more.
[From.GetFirstName]? What was I thinking!
Ignore the strange urge and look away.

Of late you have tried to live in the spirit of Valaya by treating your [From.GetHusbandWife] [From.GetTitledFirstName] with warmth. Slowly it has changed the way you are together, and those closest to you have noticed.

Of late you have tried to live in the spirit of Ptra by treating your [From.GetHusbandWife] [From.GetTitledFirstName] with respect and warmth. Slowly it has changed the way you are together, and those closest to you have noticed.

Of late you have tried to live in the spirit of Ursun by treating your [From.GetHusbandWife] [From.GetTitledFirstName] with respect and awe. Slowly it has changed the way you are together, and those closest to you have noticed.
Praised be!
Yet I cannot bring myself to touch [From.GetHerHim]...

Your [GetFromRelation], little [From.GetFirstName], has come to you with a dead bird cradled in [From.GetHerHis] arms. With a worried look [From.GetFirstName] asks what happened to it. Why is it not flying any more?
The bird is in Usirian's realm now, dearest [From.GetFirstName].
Tell §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! a gentle tale, hoping it will make [From.GetHerHim] more at ease with death.\n
Usirian is a merciless judge. Death awaits us all.
Tell §Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! the honest truth, hoping it will harden [From.GetHerHim].\n
I am busy. Go and play with the other children...

Your tale seemed to calm [From.GetTitledFirstName]. [From.GetSheHeCap] listened closely, stroking the dead bird, and when you were done [From.GetSheHe] asked some questions. Then the two of you buried the little body together in the gardens.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] listened to your tale for a while. Once it had calmed [From.GetHerHim], [From.GetSheHe] seemed to lose interest. There was no point in going on, so you sent [From.GetHerHim] off to play, and [From.GetFirstName] went without protest.

Little [From.GetFirstName] listened in silence, a serious look on [From.GetHerHis] face. Young as [From.GetSheHe] is, you could tell [From.GetSheHe] grasped something of the finality of death. [From.GetFirstName] asked some questions, and [From.GetSheHe] valued your honest answers.

Little [From.GetFirstName] listened in silence, terror on [From.GetHerHis] face. Towards the end [From.GetHerHis] lip began to quiver, but you went on, and by the time you were done [From.GetSheHe] was in tears. Perhaps you overdid it slightly...
[From.GetFirstName] will make a fine servant of Usirian one day!
[From.GetFirstName] is clearly not one of Usirian's chosen...
[From.GetFirstName] will make a fine servant of Usirian one day!
[From.GetFirstName] is clearly not one of Usirian's chosen...

A Slayer has come to your hall: a dawi with a shaved head and a great crest of orange hair, his body covered in tattoos, an axe on his shoulder. He has sworn the Slayer oath to atone for some shame he will not name, and walks north to find a death worthy of Grimnir. Tonight he asks only for ale.
Then we drink to Grimnir, and to your doom!
Let him feast like a king before he goes. The cost is mine.

The miners of [Root.Capital.GetName] have struck a seam richer than any they have seen in a generation. The old foreman swears he heard hammering deep in the rock the night before, where no dawi was working. Grungni showed them the way.
Into the treasury with it!
The first ingot goes to Grungni's shrine, forged by my own hand.

In a dream you stood in a glittering hall beneath the mountains, and an old dawi with a hammer drew a rune in the air before you, one you have never seen in any book. You woke with the shape of it burning behind your eyes.
I will set it down and study it.
Runes are not for scribbling on parchment. I will keep it secret, as the runesmiths do.

On the coldest night of the winter the hearth-fire in your hall burned so bright and so warm that the servants swore Dazh himself had come down to sit by it. The whole household slept soundly, and you woke feeling young again.
I will warm my old bones at Dazh's fire!
Open the hall. Let the cold and hungry share Dazh's fire tonight.

A merchant has come to you with an offer: a share in a caravan of furs bound for the south, at a price that seems far too good. Kalita, they say, favours the bold. Kalita, they also say, is the god of liars.
Kalita favours the bold. I will take the bargain!
Too good to be true. I will keep my gold.

Two of your subjects have brought a bitter dispute over a well before you: a father accuses his neighbour of poisoning it, and the neighbour swears it was the drought. The whole court watches to see how a follower of Phakth will judge.
The law is the law. The guilty will pay in full.
The drought was hard on them both. Let mercy temper the judgement.
Your name as a devout follower of Grimnir has spread across the land. Many great and seasoned warriors have travelled to [Root.Capital.GetName] to pledge themselves to your cause.
Your name as a devout follower of Tor has spread across the land. Many great and seasoned warriors have travelled to [Root.Capital.GetName] to pledge themselves to your cause.
Your name as a devout follower of Phakth has spread across the land. Many great and seasoned warriors have travelled to [Root.Capital.GetName] to pledge themselves to your cause.
Glory to the war god!

In your wish to be more like good Valaya you have begun to treat everyone who crosses your path with more understanding and respect. You are known now for your compassion and your noble ways, and some even call you "the Voice of Valaya".

In your wish to be more like fatherly Ursun you have begun to treat everyone who crosses your path with more understanding and respect. You are known now for your bearing and your noble ways, and some even call you "the Voice of Ursun".
I am proud to bring honour to my god.

Your work to make the most of Grungni's sacred stone has made you an example to your people. Their hard work and the rich ore the ancestors have granted have made this the best year in the mines for a generation. Feasts in Grungni's honour are held in every hold.

Your work to make the most of Dazh's sacred sun has made you an example to your people. Their hard work and the warmth the god has granted have brought the richest harvest in years. Feasts in Dazh's honour are held in every village.
Your work to rule Ptra's sacred land well has made you an example to your people. Their hard work and the god's favour have brought a year of rich floods and full granaries. Praised be Ptra!
The prosperity of [Root.Capital.GetName] is a fine sight indeed!

Following in the footsteps of Kalita has led you down many paths you would never otherwise have walked. The things one overhears on such paths are often valuable indeed. Just now you learned that [patron_plotter.GetTitledFirstName] is plotting against [patron_plot_target.GetTitledFirstName]...

Following in the footsteps of Kalita has led you down many paths you would never otherwise have walked. The things one overhears on such paths are often valuable indeed. Just now you learned that [patron_plotter.GetTitledFirstName] is plotting against none other than you!

Keeping the rites of Usirian has led you down many paths you would never otherwise have walked. The things one overhears on such paths are often valuable indeed. Just now you learned that [patron_plotter.GetTitledFirstName] is plotting against [patron_plot_target.GetTitledFirstName]...

Keeping the rites of Usirian has led you down many paths you would never otherwise have walked. The things one overhears on such paths are often valuable indeed. Just now you learned that [patron_plotter.GetTitledFirstName] is plotting against none other than you!
That treacherous snake!
Perhaps I should warn [patron_plot_target.GetHerHim].
If it is the god's will.

In your search for wisdom in the name of Thungni you have had more than one flash of insight touching the welfare of your lands. Spreading that knowledge is not only good rule but a sacred duty in itself.

In your search for wisdom in the name of Asaph you have had more than one flash of insight touching the welfare of your lands. Spreading that knowledge is not only good rule but a sacred duty in itself.
Wisdom is a bottomless well. Praised be the god!

Your [From.GetJobTitle], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has proposed that you raise a great monument to show the might of [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName]. It would have its benefits, but it would be costly, and you would need a great many hands to build it.

Your [From.GetJobTitle], [From.GetTitledFirstName], has proposed that the masons of the hold carve a great monument into the living rock to show the might of [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName]. It would stand as long as the mountain, but it would be costly, and you would need a great many hands to cut it.
I shall raise a monument in honour of Grungni.
I shall raise a monument in honour of Grimnir.
I shall raise a monument in honour of Valaya.
I shall raise a monument in honour of Thungni.
I shall raise a monument in honour of Ursun.
I shall raise a monument in honour of Dazh.
I shall raise a monument in honour of Kalita.
I shall raise a monument in honour of Tor.
I shall raise a monument in honour of Ptra.
I shall raise a monument in honour of Asaph.
I shall raise a monument in honour of Phakth.
I shall raise a monument in honour of Usirian.

When the monument is finished in a year, §Y[Root.GetTitledFirstName]§! gains §G250§! piety and §Y[Root.Capital.GetName]§! gains '§YHoly Monument§!' for as long as §Y[Root.GetTitledFirstName]§! holds it: monthly piety §G+10.0%§!.\n\n
A monument to my house and my ancestors. What an excellent idea!

When the monument is finished in a year, §Y[Root.GetTitledFirstName]§! gains §G250§! prestige and §Y[Root.Capital.GetName]§! gains '§YAncestral Monument§!' for as long as §Y[Root.GetTitledFirstName]§! holds it: monthly prestige §G+10.0%§!.\n\n
I cannot spare the gold, nor the hands...

The monument is finished at last, just as you imagined it or even finer. A great ceremony was held in honour of house [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName] and its forefathers, and what a ceremony it was! Tales of it will be told for as long as the monument stands watch over [Root.Capital.GetName].
